item.title: Government launches Malta's second National AI Strategy with 86 measures for 2026-2030
item.description: Economy Minister Silvio Schembri unveiled the strategy while opening the TECHXPO technology exhibition, saying it sets out 86 measures for 2026-2030 aimed at citizens, businesses, public institutions and researchers, and underpins the Malta Vision 2050 goals. He said around 80% of the actions under the first AI strategy had already been implemented, and that the new document places public trust at the centre of how Malta develops and uses artificial intelligence. The strategy was drawn up after a consultation involving more than 25 experts, over 70 individual stakeholders and feedback from more than 100 entities, with over 350 people taking part in seven public consultations, and it also covers widening access to AI training and computing infrastructure.

item.title: Enemalta lays six kilometres of new cables to reinforce Birkirkara's electricity network
item.description: Enemalta has installed around six kilometres of new 11kV cables across Birkirkara, replacing sections prone to faults and adding roughly 600 metres of low-voltage feeders. Energy Minister Miriam Dalli, who visited the site with Enemalta and Birkirkara council representatives, said the works address current demand while anticipating future needs. The project forms part of the company's nine-year plan to reinforce, renew and expand the distribution network across Malta and Gozo, covering cables, feeders, substations and distribution centres.

item.title: PN demands urgent talks after hotel licence fee and eco-contribution hikes
item.description: The Nationalist Party said the budget's higher hotel licence fees and tourism eco-contribution increases were announced without proper consultation with operators, calling for urgent talks with sector associations. The Malta Hotels and Restaurants Association separately warned that rising licence fees, increased eco-contributions and the cost of employing third-country nationals risk undermining Malta's tourism competitiveness.

item.title: Gozo Tourism Association proposes flat €4 eco-contribution for all accommodation
item.description: The GTA wants a flat €4 per person per night levy across all tourist accommodation in Gozo, a six-month postponement of the new rates until 1 July 2027, and a cap at seven nights per stay. It says the budget's increase of the eco-contribution from €1.50 to €8 per night for hotels and €10 for short lets, from 1 January, has already triggered booking cancellations for 2027.

item.title: Documentary 'Dear Decision Makers' brings hidden stories behind Malta's abortion laws to the screen
item.description: A new documentary by the grassroots campaign Dear Decision Makers explores pregnancy, abortion and reproductive healthcare in Malta through anonymous testimonies, animation and interviews with activists. Co-directed by Rosie Litterick and Sandie Von Brockdorff, the film builds on the campaign's collection of testimonies since 2021 and aims to put real lives behind the ongoing political debate.

item.title: Nurses say foreign staff are being recruited out of Malta to Australia, Ireland and the UK
item.description: Nurses union representatives said Maltese nurses are being headhunted to work in Australia, Ireland and England, worsening staff shortages in the local health service. Union officials highlighted the closure of hospital wards, the influx of third-country nationals and growing pressure on staff as the main changes in recent years, and said the unions have expanded their role in protecting workers.

item.title: Two hunters caught using illegal electronic bird callers in Mellieħa
item.description: Police intervened after the Malta Rangers Unit reported the use of electronic bird callers near the White Tower in Armier, inside a Natura 2000 protected site. The rangers said one hunter fired five consecutive shots when the maximum is three, and that the callers were found after he swam out to retrieve ducks. The unit says the area is becoming a hotspot for illegal hunting.

item.title: CrediaBank launches CrediaLeasing for business productive investments
item.description: CrediaBank Group has expanded its business financing offer with CrediaLeasing, a wholly owned financial leasing subsidiary. The new unit is aimed at helping firms finance productive investments such as modern production equipment, commercial real estate and vehicles while preserving liquidity.

item.title: Joseph Muscat says MEP elections took priority over Clyde Caruana's population report
item.description: Former prime minister Joseph Muscat acknowledged that the controversial 2018 population report was discussed within his administration but said European Parliament elections and other priorities took precedence. He estimated the document was around 800 pages, which differs from Clyde Caruana's earlier description of it as nearly 300 pages long, and said the foreign workers issue was no longer the key concern.

item.title: Nine people with disabilities complete programmes for independent living and employment
item.description: Six participants completed Aġenzija Sapport's 25-week Way to Work programme and three completed Skills4Life, covering job readiness, workplace behaviour, personal care and money management, along with workplace visits and volunteering. Two participants are now seeking employment with Lino Spiteri Foundation support, while others moved into further training with MCAST and Aġenzija Żgħażagħ or started work in the family business.

item.title: Repeat offender caught gambling at casino during court-imposed curfew
item.description: Adrian Muscat, 43, a contractor from Żurrieq, was arrested after police received information that he had been seen gambling at a casino in Portomaso using another person's ID card, while he should have been observing his curfew. CCTV footage showed him gambling, and he pleaded guilty to breaching bail conditions and using a false identity. He is already facing money laundering and theft proceedings over three luxury vehicles taken from a St Julian's hotel.
